subject: Business
title: The Internet: From ARPANET to Everything
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Internet: From ARPANET to Everything.

hook.text: In 1995, Newsweek published 'The Internet? Bah!' calling it a fad. Today, 5.3 billion people use it daily.

buildup.text: The internet began as ARPANET in 1969, connecting four university computers. It was designed to survive nuclear attacks.

discovery.text: Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web in 1989, making the internet accessible to non-technical users.

twist.text: The dot-com crash of 2000 wiped out $5 trillion. Everyone said the internet was overhyped. It was just early.

climax.text: Amazon, Google, and Facebook all survived the crash and became the most valuable companies in history.

punchline.text: Revolutionary technologies always look like fads. Until they change everything.

quiz.question: What was the internet originally designed to do?
options: Connect university computers and survive nuclear attacks

details.summary: The internet evolved from ARPANET, a 1969 US military research network connecting four universities, into a global system connecting billions of devices and people. It is arguably the most disruptive innovation in history, transforming communication, commerce, entertainment, and society.
details.whyItMatters: The internet disrupted more industries simultaneously than any previous technology. Understanding its evolution from military research to global platform reveals patterns of how transformative technologies emerge, mature, and reshape civilization.
takeaways: ARPANET connected four university computers in 1969 as a military research network
The World Wide Web in 1991 made the internet accessible to ordinary people
The internet disrupted media, retail, communication, and entertainment simultaneously

faq.question: What made the World Wide Web different from the internet itself?
faq.answer: The internet is the physical network connecting computers. The World Wide Web, invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989, is an application running on the internet using hyperlinks, URLs, and browsers to make information accessible and navigable. The web made the internet usable for everyone.

faq.question: What could experts not predict about how the internet would develop?
faq.answer: Very few predicted social media, the smartphone revolution, streaming entertainment, the gig economy, e-commerce dominance, or the dark side of misinformation and surveillance. Each emerged from user behavior interacting with capabilities in ways that were difficult to foresee.
